intro: All projects are assessed with this rubric. Each project prompt lists its own technical requirements and submission items.
levels: Exemplary (A)
Proficient (B)
Developing (C)
Beginning (D/F)

criteria.name: Technical execution
levels: Meets every technical requirement in the prompt and uses the module's techniques with intention, often going beyond them; the code or patch is organized and commented, and the work runs reliably.
Meets all technical requirements; some techniques are used only minimally; the code or patch is mostly organized.
Meets most requirements; one is missing or does not work as intended.
Several requirements are missing, or the work does not run.

criteria.name: Experimentation and range
levels: Clearly explores the possibilities of the techniques and materials, testing and pushing ideas well beyond a first attempt.
Shows some exploration beyond a first attempt.
Exploration is minimal or accidental.
Little or no evidence of exploration.

criteria.name: Aesthetic discernment
levels: Makes clear, deliberate choices (composition, color, motion, space, sound) that serve the work's intent, explains those choices convincingly in critique, and takes a risk.
Choices are deliberate and mostly coherent and are explained in critique.
Choices look like defaults or go unexamined; little explanation.
No evident decisions; no explanation.

criteria.name: Critique
levels: Explains code and choices clearly; gives specific, generous feedback to at least two classmates (spoken, in chat, or in writing).
Explains the work; gives feedback to at least one classmate.
Brief explanation; minimal feedback.
Absent from critique with no alternative contribution.

note: Coding sketches and in-class exercises are graded on completion and good-faith experimentation, not perfection. Participation can take many forms: speaking, chat, private messages to me, or written responses to classmates' work.
